Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines: damages & testing

Marcus — attaching TerraLogic's counter-redline to the MSA and Order Form. High level: they will not accept a blanket prohibition on stress/benchmark testing without a damages remedy for breach; their counsel insists on injunctive relief carve-outs for IP and data misuse, and they're proposing an explicit "prohibited testing" clause with an agreed remedy (3x damages + injunctive relief for exfiltration).

Key asks from TerraLogic legal: 
- Confirm whether Redwood will accept an exception to the testing prohibition limited to documented, pre-approved benchmarking with agreed throttles.
- Consider an IP/data-related injunctive relief carve-out (they want to keep ability to seek immediate relief).
- Provide your liability cap position for the Order Form. They flagged a clause that would carve out consequential damages for certain types of testing-related losses.

I've added inline comments in TL_counter_redline_v1.docx. Please loop in your legal and procurement so we can get to a single redline quickly — they need a final by end of next week.

Thanks,

Laura / Karthik — forwarding TerraLogic's counter. They appear to be pushing for: (a) a carve-out for injunctive relief around IP/data exfil; (b) an explicit damages remedy tied to prohibited testing; and (c) clarity on the liability cap math for the Order Form.

Operational ask: we need a short set of positions we can send back (preferably plain language bullets) so Sales can keep momentum. My proposed starting positions: 
1) Cap: Redwood prefers a standard cap of the greater of (12 months' fees) or $2M for Order Forms < $5M; recommend we hold firm but be willing to move to 3x fees for strategic customers.
2) Injunctive relief: accept narrow injunctive relief for IP/data theft but require high burden (clear demonstration).
3) Prohibited testing: do not accept a pre-determined liquidated-damages multiple; instead propose expedited cure + termination + damages up to cap.

Can Legal provide language we can present? Procurement will want a clear path to close.

—Marcus

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines: damages & testing

Marcus — thanks for the summary. Draft guidance below (and attached a redline: redline_TL_v2.docx) you can send to TerraLogic with minimal edits. High-level legal positions and rationale: 

1) Liability cap: propose the cap be the greater of (12 months of fees) or $3,000,000 for the Order Form. Rationale: balances commercial risk while keeping predictable exposure. If this is a strategic/enterprise deal we can discuss a higher committed cap, but we should not default to multiples of fees (e.g., 3x) as a standard.

2) Carve-outs: accept a carve-out for (a) gross negligence and willful misconduct; (b) IP infringement and (c) remedies necessary to stop unauthorized data exfiltration (injunctive relief). For injunctive relief: we accept narrow, immediate injunctive relief for IP/data exfiltration—no open-ended exception to liability. Include a requirement that injunctive relief must be proportionate and limited to what is necessary to prevent imminent harm.

3) Prohibited testing / benchmarking: we cannot agree to a clause that automatically triggers a pre-agreed multiplier of damages for so-called prohibited testing. Instead propose: (i) define prohibited testing narrowly (unauthorized bulk extraction, adversarial model probing that attempts to reconstruct private data), (ii) provide an accelerated remediation and disablement path, and (iii) allow customer to seek equitable relief for data exfiltration and damages otherwise subject to the agreed cap. If TerraLogic insists on a liquidated damages figure, propose a capped penalty tied to actual customer fees (e.g., up to 50% of annual fees) rather than unlimited or multi-year multiples.

4) Contract language suggestion (summary to include in reply): 
- "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, each Party may seek injunctive relief for alleged infringement of its intellectual property rights or to prevent actual or imminent unauthorized data exfiltration. Such relief shall be no broader than necessary to prevent the harm alleged."
- For prohibited testing: include a short list of prohibited activities and a two-step remedy: (A) immediate suspension of offending access, (B) damages up to the Contract Cap, with the option for equitable relief for data exfiltration.

5) Next steps: I recommend we send TerraLogic a clean point-by-point letter (not a full redline yet) with the proposed compromise and invite them to accept or propose one limited change. If they push back hard on the cap, we can offer a one-time concession: cap = greater of 18 months' fees or $5M for the Order Form, limited to signed commercial commitments.

I'll be on standby if you want line edits.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Marcus / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and the constructive positions. We circulated Laura's suggested language internally and counsel is generally comfortable with the compromise. Two small items from our side: 
1) TerraLogic requests the injunctive relief carve-out explicitly reference "data exfiltration" and allow for emergency access revocation (they want the right to cut API keys pending court order). We are willing to limit scope to suspected/verified exfiltration only.
2) Regarding the cap: TerraLogic will accept Redwood's proposed compromise of the greater of 12 months' fees or $3M provided there is a mutual escalation flow and a metric for materiality — they asked for an explicit 'material breach' tie to trigger termination (w/ cure period).

If those two tweaks can be accommodated in the redline, we can accept and route to our procurement for signature next week. I've attached a final redline (TL_redline_final.docx) with the small edits. Please send a DocuSign link once you have Redwood's final clean executed copy.
